method: Historical-province polygons were downloaded from Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004 (jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0), compared to EU5 calibrated location centroids and area_jacobian_km2, and checked against Farris (2006) Table 1.3. A province was not promoted when centroid inclusion or conservative area coverage failed the >=95% contract.

records.historical_boundary: Bungo no kuni polygon, Harvard CHGIS
records.reason: Seven of eight EU5 Bungo centroids fall inside the CHGIS polygon, but the Hayami location lies outside; centroid-area coverage is only 89.94%. The area ratio alone (1.0484) cannot prove polygon overlap, so this population floor remains validation-only until exact EU5 polygon intersections or a period-correct crosswalk are supplied.
sources: Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0

records.historical_boundary: Hyūga no kuni polygon, Harvard CHGIS
records.reason: Only six of eight EU5 Hyūga centroids fall inside the CHGIS polygon; the Naka-Hyūga and Miyazaki locations are outside, leaving 82.96% centroid-area coverage. The 2.42% area-ratio difference is insufficient to establish overlap. Retain the Farris floor for diagnostics but do not train on it.
sources: Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0

records.historical_boundary: Satsuma no kuni polygon, Harvard CHGIS
records.reason: All four EU5 Satsuma centroids fall inside the historical polygon, but the calibrated EU5 union covers only 94.21% of the historical polygon area. The missing area is too large for the >=95% training contract, so no lower-bound label is promoted without a sub-location area-weighted intersection.
sources: Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0

records.historical_boundary: Ōsumi no kuni polygon, Harvard CHGIS
records.reason: Only five of seven EU5 Ōsumi centroids fall inside the CHGIS polygon; two island/peninsular locations lie outside and centroid-area coverage is 75.38%. The 16.45% area overhang is not acceptable for a training floor.
sources: Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0

records.historical_boundary: Hizen no kuni polygon, Harvard CHGIS
records.reason: The EU5 Hizen union is 37.44% larger than the historical Hizen polygon, and the CHGIS polygon includes a complex island/coastal outline not represented by the coarse EU5 selector. A name match cannot support a >=95% historical-boundary crosswalk.
sources: Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0

records.historical_boundary: Wakasa no kuni polygon, Harvard CHGIS
records.reason: The EU5 geometry inventory has no dedicated Wakasa province. Assigning the historical province to Echizen would silently replace a 905 km2 historical polygon with a much larger modern/game grouping, so the record remains unmapped.
sources: Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004, DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0
